excerpt: **Citibank, N.A.** (stylized as **citi**bank; "N.A." stands for "[National Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_bank_(United_States) "National bank (United States)")") is the primary U.S. banking subsidiary of [Citigroup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citigroup "Citigroup"), a [financial services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_services "Financial services") [multinational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinational_corporation "Multinational corporation") corporation.[[2]](#cite_note-2) Citibank was founded in 1812 as **City Bank of New York**, and later became **First National City Bank of New York**.[[3]](#cite_note-3) The bank has [branches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branch_(banking) "Branch (banking)") in 19 countries.[[1]](#cite_note-10K-1) The U.S. branches are concentrated in six metropolitan areas: [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), and [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami "Miami"). Citibank used to maintain a longtime presence in the [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston") metropolitan area, but withdrew from their seventh major market in 2016.[[1]](#cite_note-10K-1)[[4]](#cite_note-4)
